name: Gerstmann Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Gerstmann Syndrome

criteria.description: Inability to recognize or differentiate fingers on the hand
Impairment in writing ability despite intact motor function
Inability to distinguish left from right on oneself or others
Lesion localized to the dominant parietal lobe, especially angular gyrus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all four major symptoms (finger agnosia, agraphia, acalculia, left-right disorientation)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by neuroimaging findings; exclusion of other causes is necessary.

pathognomonic.notes: Core symptom reflecting parietal lobe dysfunction
Impaired writing ability despite preserved motor skills

common.notes: Difficulty with spatial orientation and perception

occasional.notes: Difficulty in drawing or constructing objects
Confusion extends to distinguishing left and right on others
Short-term memory deficits may be present
Difficulty with more complex mathematical tasks

rare.notes: Weakness on one side of the body in some cases

imaging: MRI showing lesion or infarct in dominant parietal lobe, especially angular gyrus
CT scan may reveal ischemic changes in relevant cortical areas
genetic: Rare familial cases reported; possible autosomal dominant inheritance in some
other: Neuropsychological testing confirms deficits in calculation, writing, finger recognition, and left-right orientation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of alexia (reading impairment) alongside agraphia
Lesions typically involve left angular gyrus but with additional language deficits
Optic ataxia, oculomotor apraxia, and simultanagnosia
Bilateral parietal-occipital lesions rather than unilateral
Sudden onset and imaging consistent with vascular event

redFlags: Sudden onset of symptoms suggesting stroke
references: Damasio AR, Damasio H. Gerstmann syndrome: a clinical and anatomical study. Arch Neurol. 1979.
Karnath HO, et al. The anatomy of Gerstmann syndrome. Brain. 2005.
Benson DF, et al. The angular gyrus syndrome. Neurology. 1979.
